name: red-team

findings.message: The `parallel.group.complete` event emits `verdict=pass` for groups where all members had `fail` outcomes (because `_ZB_MAP_UNFINISHED` tracks only unfinished outcomes, not `fail`), immediately before the new guard stops the pipeline with `pipeline.end status=failed`; event consumers see group-pass followed by pipeline-failed with no intermediate state, which is introduced here for the `on_member_error=continue` (runner default) + all-fail case that previously continued to pr-delivery.

SPEC-4 only has a runtime assertion for the stop path (`ZBUILD_RUN_FLAGGED=yes` → `_update_stage_status` not called); R4 (all pass → guard does NOT fire and `_update_stage_status` IS called) has no runtime behavioral test, so a guard condition inverted to `!= no` or `!= yes` would pass all existing assertions while silently breaking the all-pass path.

The new guard (lines 3731-3742) calls both `_set_pipeline_status` and `_zbuild_state_set_stage_verdict`, but the existing rc-failure path (lines 3718-3727) calls `_set_pipeline_status` only; `stage_verdicts` in the state file has a `failed` entry when the new guard fires but no entry when the rc-check fires, so downstream readers of stage verdicts observe asymmetric state depending on which failure path is taken.

The error message falls back to the generic string `a member did not pass` when `_ZB_MAP_UNFINISHED` is empty, which occurs whenever all non-passing members had `fail` outcomes (finish = pass or fail); the message omits which members failed and their outcome, reducing diagnostic value for the `fail` case under `on_member_error=continue`.

The `outcome != pass` change applies to all map groups globally, not just review groups; a non-review map group (e.g. build-platforms) with a `timed_out` member under the runner's default `on_member_error=continue` now stops the pipeline immediately where the prior code would have continued, expanding the scope of the fix beyond the issue's stated intent of review lenses.

reason: the red-team lens found no high or critical problem the change introduced that fails it
